title: Acceptance versus completion
explanation: The command is accepted for later handling; success remains unestablished.
limit: No HTTP request or worker execution.

title: Polling interval trade-off
explanation: The idealised worst observation delay is close to the interval; shortening it increases request frequency.
limit: Finite arithmetic model, no network traffic.

title: One-way push
explanation: The direction requirement is server-to-client updates, so a bidirectional channel is not automatically necessary.

title: Bidirectional channel duties
explanation: WebSocket may fit, but authentication, validation, reconnect and cleanup remain required.
limit: Decision aid, not a universal recommendation.

title: Compound key collision
explanation: Naïve colon concatenation collides; tuple encoding keeps the pairs distinct.
limit: Derived key demonstration, not production identity.

title: Replacement cleanup
explanation: Late cleanup removes the registry entry only when the closing socket is still current.

title: Targeted delivery
explanation: Delivery uses both correlation and trusted recipient identity; broadcast is not an acceptable shortcut.

title: 202 without status route
explanation: A Location value alone does not create a status resource.

title: Enqueue failure
explanation: The API must not emit acceptance metadata after queue failure.

title: Minimal job payload
explanation: Only data required by the worker belongs in the queued message.
limit: Design classification, not a privacy audit.

title: Monotonic progress
explanation: 10 is rejected, equal 25 adds no new progress and 40 advances.
limit: Reference currently republishes equal progress; no BullMQ event.

title: Terminal stability
explanation: A terminal projection must not reopen.

title: Completion shape
explanation: Missing result fields should not silently become a successful completed descriptor.

title: Owner-scoped job ID
explanation: Acceptance and projection ownership must refer to the same job identity.

title: Pending before send
explanation: The pending entry must exist before send so a synchronous reply can settle it.

title: Reverse reply order
explanation: Each result resolves the promise selected by request ID, not arrival position.

title: Timeout is local
explanation: The caller stopped waiting. Remote cancellation is unestablished without a protocol command.

title: Close state
explanation: A dispatcher policy should define whether later dispatch is rejected immediately.

title: ID reuse window
explanation: A late old reply is indistinguishable after ID reuse unless the protocol includes a generation or non-reuse policy.

title: Dispose cleanup
explanation: The terminal invariant is zero owned resources and refusal of new work.
limit: Expected end-state model, not actual P03 execution.
